ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, s. 462.31; Limited Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 227, as amended; Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, Part 9.1 (corporate transparency register); United Nations Act, S.C. 2000, c. 27; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 22; and FINTRAC issued guidance on customer due diligence and beneficial ownership.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (BC registry maintains limited public corporate information, but beneficial ownership data in the LP transparency record is not publicly searchable; access is restricted to authorized regulatory and law-enforcement authorities, with additional disclosures allowed only by court order or specific statutory authority).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry in the partner's country of origin (e.g., provincial/state corporate registry or federal companies office, as applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in country of origin and Hague Apostille for use in Canada (Canada implemented the Apostille Convention effective 11 January 2024; for non-fulfilling states, consular legalization remains required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of constitutional documents, charter documents, and corporate resolutions authorizing appointment of the BC general partner and establishing the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary / legal counsel of the foreign corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the issuing state; or consular legalization where apostille not available

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and proof-of-residence for each individual beneficial owner / limited partner, with certified English or French translation where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and, where available, Hague Apostille; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or legal opinion confirming the authority of signatories and directors binding the foreign corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Outside counsel / corporate secretary of the foreign entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille unless the opinion is issued by a British Columbia lawyer in Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, general partners, designated limited partners and persons with significant control must be screened against Canada's Consolidated Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act regulations, and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act lists. PEP determination follows the FATF definition (senior political figures, their family members and close associates) under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance. For USD wire and ACH payment rails, additional best-effort screening against the U.S. OFAC SDN list is standard practice to avoid correspondent banking blockages. A wholesale liquidation LP does not require a statutory license under BC law, so no FINTRAC compliance program is mandatory unless ancillary services such as money transmission are added; banks and payment processors will nevertheless impose contractual AML/CFT obligations on the LP.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act, S.B.C. 2019, c. 7 (in force November 1, 2021), as amended; Partnership Act Regulation (prescribed forms and fees); Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 (default rules where the general partner is a corporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Registry Division, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (prescribed form filed under the Limited Partnership Act; registered in the corporate register of British Columbia).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. Limited partners must contribute cash, property, or agreed value as recorded in the Limited Partnership Agreement; the general partner manages the contributions in trust and records each limited partner's capital account for pass-through tax allocation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [LP NAME] LIMITED PARTNERSHIP ADOPTED [DATE]

BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. The filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the Registrar of Companies is approved, and the General Partner is authorized to execute and deliver such instrument.
2. The registered office and records address of the Partnership shall be [address], British Columbia.
3. [Name] is appointed as the general partner, and [Name] as authorized agent, with authority to open bank accounts and execute banking resolutions.
4. Capital contributions of the limited partners are accepted as set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement.

This resolution is effective forthwith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a computer-assisted NUANS name search through the BC Registries online portal. Submit a Name Request containing the proposed name with the legal element 'Limited Partnership' (or 'LP'/'L.P.') and up to three alternative names. Pay the prescribed name request fee and retain the reservation number. The reservation is valid for 56 calendar days and is renewable for an additional 56 days before filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the name on grounds of confusing similarity or prohibited elements, refile a revised Name Request with a distinguishing element, or submit a written appeal to the Corporate Registry's name review within 30 days of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration Dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel or notary public; no government filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement recording capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, management powers of the general partner, and dissolution events. Complete the Declaration of Limited Partnership with the statutory particulars, including the registered office address in British Columbia, mailing address, full names and addresses of all general partners, and confirmations of limited partner contributions. Signatures must be witnessed; if a signatory is outside Canada, the signature must be notarized or commissioned by a local notary with an apostille where applicable.
required_dossiers: Executed Declaration of Limited Partnership (prescribed form)
Consent to Act as General Partner
Certificate of Status/certified copy of incorporation of the corporate general partner, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Declaration is factually incomplete, prepare and re-execute corrected pages with clean signatures and resubmit before the name reservation expires; if notarization is deficient, obtain a replacement notarial certificate from the commissioning notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries — Corporate Registry (online bconline filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the BC Registries online service, select the limited partnership registration/filing function under the Limited Partnership Act, upload or enter the executed Declaration of Limited Partnership, attach the Consent to Act and any GP incorporation certificate, and pay the prescribed filing fee (approximately CAD 40 equivalent) by Visa, Mastercard, or authorized debit. Retain the electronic payment receipt and the filing acknowledgement bearing the registration date and file number.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as General Partner / authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or returned for correction, respond to the Registrar's deficiency letter within 30 days; for substantive defects, file an Amended/Corrected Declaration with the prescribed correction fee, retaining the original registration priority date where the statute permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Limited Partnership and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries (Corporate Registry); Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance; WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: On registration, download and retain the Certificate of Limited Partnership (or electronic registry acknowledgement). Register for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) service, including GST/HST account if worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000. Register for the BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) account if taxable retail sales are made in BC, and register with WorkSafeBC before any employees or contractors commence work. Notify CRA that the entity status is a limited partnership with the corporate or individual general partner as the designated agent.
required_dossiers: CRA RC1 form / BRO online application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or the BC tax authorities reject the account applications, correct the missing registration data in the BRO or eTaxBC portal and resubmit; if a BN is delayed, the LP may continue operations using the partnership name while providing the pending BN reference on invoices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Statutory Books, and Annual Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian bank (e.g., RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO) and BC Registries annual reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a business bank account in the name of the limited partnership by presenting the Certificate of Limited Partnership, the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, the general partner resolution authorizing account opening, and government-issued photo identification of all principals; complete the bank's AML/KYC form and beneficial ownership declaration. Establish the statutory books (register of limited partners, resolutions, capital contribution records) at the registered office. Diarize the annual report filing due within two months after each anniversary of registration.
required_dossiers: General Partner Resolution authorizing banking arrangements
Government-issued photo identification of the general partner and beneficial owners
Completed bank KYC / AML declaration and proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide a notarized beneficial ownership chain, a certificate of good standing from BC Registries, and the LP agreement's capital contribution schedule; if an annual report is filed late, pay the prescribed late fee online to restore good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the off-price wholesale and liquidation of finished branded apparel is a distribution/warehousing trade (ISIC 4641 / NAICS 424320), not a manufacturing or heavy-industrial facility; no provincial industrial licensing board or industrial permit is prescribed for this activity in British Columbia.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no province-wide operating permit is mandated for apparel wholesale liquidation. The operator must, however, obtain a municipal business licence from the local government where the business premises are situated (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence) and comply with zoning for wholesale storage and distribution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (British Columbia) — Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — wholesale warehousing of finished garments is not a reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act (S.B.C. 2018, c. 3) and the Reviewable Projects Regulation; no EIA certificate, environmental impact statement, or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to pure wholesale trading. If the premises include ancillary garment treatment (e.g., laundering, pressing, or dyeing), wastewater and air discharges must meet municipal sewer bylaws and the Environmental Management Act (S.B.C. 2003, c. 53); otherwise, only ordinary municipal solid waste handling rules and indoor air/fire code thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational health and safety clearance under the Workers Compensation Act and WorkSafeBC regulations; fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code for warehouse/storage occupancy; structural load inspections for pallet racking under the BC Building Code; municipal building occupancy certificate for the premises. Civil-defense-specific clearances are not required.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (monetary authority); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) (prudential supervision of Schedule I banks); Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) (AML/CFT transaction reporting); Global Affairs Canada (economic sanctions administration). Canada has no separate foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control bureaucracy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible. Current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted; inward equity contributions to and profit remittances from a British Columbia limited partnership require no central-bank approval or convertibility license. Non-resident partner distributions may be subject to Canadian tax, withholding, and reporting obligations, but not exchange-control barriers. Payments to sanctioned jurisdictions/parties are restricted by Canadian economic sanctions law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no surrender requirement, no mandatory deduction, and no conversion timeline for export proceeds. A BC exporter may invoice in CAD, USD, or other freely convertible currencies and may retain foreign currency abroad or in domestic foreign-currency bank accounts. FINTRAC reporting applies to electronic funds transfers of C$10,000 or more, and commercial transaction records should evidence the underlying garment purchase and resale to prevent trade-based money laundering.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary regulated banking corridor. Foreign electronic-money institutions (EMIs) are not chartered banks in Canada and cannot provide OSFI-regulated deposit accounts. A non-resident EMI may be used only as a secondary payment aggregator/wallet in its own jurisdiction, subject to its licensing, and should not hold Canadian client funds or present itself as a Canadian bank. Correspondent concentration with a tier-1 Canadian bank remains the compliant route.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statute requires directors or partners to appear physically at a Canadian bank branch. Remote/video-onboarding is permitted when the bank's CDD program captures valid government-issued ID, liveness, and documentary records. In practice, Schedule I banks frequently require a video interview or notarized/certified true copy for non-resident signatories and beneficial owners; in-person attendance is not mandatory, but should be offered if the bank's enterprise policy demands it for the LP's general partner or U.S.-resident principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership in the limited partnership structure when no individual holds a clear 25%+ interest or control is split among non-resident limited partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed limited partnership agreement; current register of individuals with significant control; organizational chart from ultimate beneficial owners through each intermediate entity; proof of identity and residential address for all 25%+ partners; general partner declaration of control; certificate of existence/good standing from BC Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP status, or adverse-country exposure arising from supplier/payment jurisdictions used for overstock apparel sourcing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global Affairs Canada sanctions screening results for all parties; independent open-source adverse-media report; PEP declarations for every beneficial owner; fund-sourcing explanation supported by bank statements and audited/compiled financial statements; jurisdiction-specific legal entity due diligence for each supplier jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border trade payments without visible nexus to physical goods, triggering trade-based money-laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and sales contracts; commercial invoices; packing lists; bills of lading/waybills; customs entry forms (Canada CBSA), inspection certificates; payment reconciliation schedule matching invoices to MT103 remittances; supplier onboarding file confirming vendor existence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party payments or encrypted/fast-payment channels inconsistent with the stated wholesale liquidation business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written ACH/SWIFT-only payment policy; third-party payment register identifying purpose, contractual basis, and ultimate counterparty; prohibition of cash and virtual-currency settlement for trade disbursements; annual compliance attestation by the general partner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity/capital injections should be routed as SWIFT MT103 payments from the foreign parent/limited partner to the BC LP's tier-1 Canadian bank account. The wire must reference the LP's legal name, the designated account number, and a clear purpose description such as 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION / LP CAPITAL CALL'. Supporting documentation for the bank file should include the capital call notice, LP agreement, source of funds in the remitting account, and a Canadian filing/record confirming the LP registration. FINTRAC EFT reporting obligations are generally discharged by the bank, but the LP must maintain its own records of all inbound transfers of C$10,000 or more. There is no Canadian FX approval requirement; USD funds may settle through Fedwire/CHIPS and be converted to CAD at market rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments for finished garments should be made by SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) or by commercial letter of credit (UCP600) for documentary shipments. For domestic Canadian suppliers, Payments Canada ACH/credit-push and EFT rails are accepted. USD vendor payments may be cleared through the Canadian bank's U.S. correspondent network (Fedwire/ACH). Each disbursement should carry the invoice number, purchase order and a payment purpose code/text indicating 'GOODS TRADE PAYMENT / TEXTILES'; the underlying transport and customs documents must be retained to substantiate the trade pipeline and satisfy bank monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot USD/CAD contract for immediate settlement
Deliverable FX forward for locked USD/CAD conversion at a set maturity
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for emerging-market currency exposures where delivery is impracticable
Vanilla FX call/put option to protect budgeted fabric and logistics costs
Cross-currency swap (CAD/USD) for spanning liquidity across the wholesale liquidation cycle

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Report (status confirmation and registered particulars)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance (Province of British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: due within two months after the annual anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in British Columbia.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a CAD 100 late fee; failure to file and pay for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and deemed dissolution of the limited partnership under the BC Partnership Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and applicable partnership schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end: on or before March 31 of the following calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal period, within three months after the fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or failure to file exposes the partnership and partners to Income Tax Act s. 162 penalties (per-partner monthly penalty), daily interest, and potential gross-negligence penalties; no CRA strike-off applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit threshold for a private BC limited partnership under the Partnership Act; an independent audit becomes mandatory only if required by the partnership agreement, a court order, lender covenants, or BC securities law for a reporting-issuer partnership.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian ASPE (private enterprise) or IFRS as adopted by CPA Canada, depending on the partnership agreement; tax accounting follows Income Tax Act fiscal-period rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: British Columbia does not maintain a standing UBO annual-filing regime for limited partnerships. Transfers of partnership interests must be recorded in the limited partners' register when executed and reflected in the next annual report; any change to the general partner or registered particulars must be amended with BC Registries without waiting for the annual cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (contributions, profit-sharing ratios, and capital withdrawals)
Register of General Partners and management authority
Minute Book containing consents, resolutions, and partnership decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 150–CAD 400 (USD 110–300) annually for a BC registered office address and registered services via a registered agent or law firm.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 2,500–CAD 7,500 (USD 1,900–5,700) for a private LP year-end compilation/review; a full GAAS audit can reach USD 10,000–20,000 for merchandise-heavy wholesale operations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (15% federal + 12% British Columbia provincial) for general corporations; limited partnership is pass-through, partners taxed at individual or corporate rates
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction: federal 9% on first CAD 500,000, BC 2% on first CAD 500,000 (combined 11%) for Canadian-controlled private corporations; limited partnership not eligible as it is not a corporation

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 - Partnership Information Return, filed electronically via CRA's e-file (EFILE) or NETFILE for partnerships
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, due by May 31 of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name and business number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full legal name and Canadian business number (BN) if registered; non-resident partners must be identified with their foreign tax identification number
Indicate the fiscal period end date; non-resident partners must align with the partnership's fiscal year for reporting

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income/loss to each partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report each partner's share of income/loss; non-resident partners must receive a T5013 slip and may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax on Canadian-source income
Use NAICS 424320 for off-price wholesale liquidation; ensure consistency with CRA industry codes

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: CAD 100 per month per partner (up to 12 months, maximum CAD 2,500 per partner); additional penalties for gross negligence (5% of unreported income plus 50% of tax evaded) and criminal prosecution for willful evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-residents; for limited partnership distributions to non-resident partners, the withholding tax applies to the partner's share of Canadian-source income at a rate of 25% (Part XIII of the Income Tax Act)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident partner must provide the partnership with a completed NR301 (for individuals) or NR302 (for corporations) form, along with a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the partner's home tax authority. The partnership must withhold at the reduced treaty rate only after receiving these documents. For Canada-U.S. treaty, the rate on business profits is generally 0% if no permanent establishment; for dividends, 5% or 15% depending on shareholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 25%, interest 25% (Part XIII). Treaty rates: royalties typically 10% (e.g., U.S., U.K.), interest often 0% for arm's length transactions (e.g., U.S., U.K.) or 10% for non-arm's length. Must apply treaty via NR301/NR302 and TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Transactions with non-resident related parties exceeding CAD 1 million (goods) or CAD 500,000 (services, interest, royalties, etc.) trigger mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) under Section 247 of the Income Tax Act
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and treaty abuse provisions (e.g., under BEPS MLI) require genuine economic substance. Partnerships must demonstrate real business activities, employees, and premises to avoid recharacterization of transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false deductions, or deliberate misrepresentation of partnership allocations to non-resident partners to avoid Canadian tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act: fine up to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties: 50% of tax evaded plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they fail to withhold and remit; travel bans and seizure of personal assets may be imposed

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a limited partnership with no real business activity, employees, or physical presence in Canada, used solely to route profits to non-residents without substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment: disallowance of treaty benefits, additional tax at 25% withholding, and penalties up to 10% of the tax avoided; CRA may also impose a 5% penalty for failure to file T5013
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners may be held personally liable for all taxes, interest, and penalties if the partnership is deemed a sham; travel bans and asset freezes under the Tax Collection Act

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a money services business (MSB) if the partnership engages in remittance or currency exchange; or failing to report suspicious transactions under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1 million for individuals and CAD 2 million for entities; criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment for willful non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally fined up to CAD 500,000 and imprisoned for up to 5 years; personal assets may be subject to forfeiture if involved in money laundering
